description:
Michael restated the concept on 2026-10-08: an episode's locations in the Fabula graph form the spine of a generative IF adventure, with LLM-as-DM supplying grounded content on demand and a deterministic engine persisting it, so the game writes itself into durable existence. He then directed "build the wolf hall projection experiment". This supersedes T-040's Gate 0 paper playtest as the next step: that gate tested an authored three-event Dracula mystery, not whether the graph can spine a generated world.

Built (commit 137d917, plus the Happy Valley follow-up): adventure/projection.py reads a published episode from Postgres into a JSON world keyed by fabula_uuid; adventure/explore.py is a deterministic engine where position is a moment, next/back step the episode, and go to <place> jumps to that place's next recorded moment; look/watch/examine passages are written once and persisted, and the parser never substitutes a target. adventure/narrator.py renders observational packets verbatim (local) or paraphrased (openrouter), with source pointers. adventure/scenarios.py serves both the Dracula prototype (unchanged routes, session key and saves) and projected worlds from settings.ADVENTURE_WORLDS at /play/<slug>/. world_report management command prints coverage. Also fixed UTF-8 mojibake in chat/llm.py, which affected Ask the Archive.

Results (docs/WOLF_HALL_PROJECTION.md): Wolf Hall S01E01 (87 moments, 27 rooms) and Happy Valley S01E01 (85 moments, 43 rooms) are walkable end to end with zero hand authoring; the second series needed only a settings line. Findings: going to a place is also a jump in time and over half of rooms hold one moment, so the spine is events at places; primary locations can be coarse buckets (25 of 87 Wolf Hall moments in one room); location identity is split under different names in both series; EventPage.description, Location.description and analytical involvement fields leak later events and are evidence-only; possessive names needed general parser fixes (owner names, dash prefixes, containment tiebreak); presence looks fused across scenes in Happy Valley moments 22-23 (UP-009 class, unverified); the offline download reaches 6.2 MB.

Central gap against the concept: accepted passages are saved per visitor playthrough only. A new visitor starts with every passage unwritten, and with the LLM author each visitor pays for the same passages again under a 12-call cap per save. The world does not yet write itself into a shared, durable game. Proposed next step: a world-level passage store keyed by world, passage key and source-packet hash; playthroughs keep only position and visits; changed source retires the passage; an acceptance policy for LLM passages; the model budget moves to the world.

Verification: 108 adventure+chat tests pass (21 new on a fixture episode). Real-data sessions through the API on both worlds. Six live OpenRouter calls, capped at six. Offline download content/syntax checked, not browser-tested. Not deployed; ADVENTURE_ENABLED is off in production.

Open: shared world-level passages (above); unfamiliar-reader play on a projected world; share repeated blocks in the offline edition; decide moment vs room-at-a-moment position; file identity splits and fused presence upstream once the graph can be queried with properties() evidence.
title: Project episodes from the graph into walkable adventure worlds (Wolf Hall, Happy Valley)
